elaeagnus-umbellata.summary: Autumn olive is a spreading deciduous shrub with silvery foliage, fragrant pale flowers and small red fruits dotted with pale scales. Native to Asia, it was widely planted in the United States for landscaping and erosion control. Birds and small mammals carry its seeds into fields, roadsides and woodland edges. Its roots can add nitrogen to the soil, helping it grow on poor ground. In North Carolina and other affected regions, dense growth can crowd surrounding vegetation.

zephyranthes-candida.summary: Autumn zephyrlily is a small bulb-forming perennial with narrow green leaves and white, crocuslike flowers. Blooms rise above the grassy foliage in summer and autumn, often following rain. It comes from South America and is grown widely as an ornamental in borders and containers. The plants form compact clumps, and offsets develop around the original bulbs. In mild climates the leaves may remain green; in colder places the bulbs need protection from winter freezing.

chenopodium-hircinum.summary: Chenopodium hircinum is an annual herb from South America and a wild relative of quinoa. Its upright stems branch near the base, carrying alternate leaves that often have three uneven lobes. A pale, mealy coating and an unpleasant smell are useful supporting clues. The tiny whitish-green flowers grow in clusters along narrow spikes. Leaf shape varies considerably, so a familiar-looking leaf alone is not enough to separate it from other goosefoots; mature seeds can be important for identification.

sources.label: Mosyakin and colleagues: Lectotypification of Chenopodium hircinum
PROCISUR: Dinámica de poblaciones y control de malezas en soja, p.167

persea-americana.summary: Avocado is an evergreen tree from tropical America, grown for fleshy fruits with a single large seed. Its broad leaves form a dense crown, while small greenish-yellow flowers appear in branching clusters. Fruit size, skin texture and ripening season vary considerably among cultivated varieties. The trees grow best in warm, sunny places with good soil drainage. Avocados have been cultivated in the Americas since before European contact and remain an important orchard crop in tropical and subtropical regions.

sources.label: UF/IFAS: Avocado Growing in the Florida Home Landscape

pseudacysta-perseae.summary: Avocado lace bug is a tiny leaf-feeding insect whose translucent wing covers resemble fine lace. Adults and spiny young gather beneath avocado leaves, where their feeding creates pale patches that can turn brown. Dark specks of waste and clusters of eggs are useful clues on the lower leaf surface. The insect also uses some other plants in the laurel family. Heavy infestations can cause early leaf drop, exposing fruit and branches to sun; small populations may cause little lasting damage.

fiorinia-fioriniae.summary: Avocado scale is a small armored scale insect found on avocado, palms, tea and many other plants. Females sit beneath narrow, light-brown covers, often lined up along veins on the undersides of leaves. Their feeding can leave yellow spots, and heavy infestations may weaken foliage. Young mobile stages move to new feeding sites, while infested nursery plants can carry established colonies farther afield. Several related scales look very similar, so a microscope is usually needed to confirm the species.

sources.label: Watson: Diaspididae of the World—Fiorinia fioriniae
University of Hawaii: Insect and Mite Pests of Tea, p. 8

froggattiella-penicillata.summary: Froggattiella penicillata is a small armored scale insect associated with bamboo and other grasses. Females live beneath elongated protective covers, often tucked under leaf sheaths where they are easy to overlook. A Korean study found colonies on the stems of Sasa bamboo and described yellow covers with a darker yellow tip. Closely related scales can look similar without magnification. Its life history and economic effects remain poorly understood, so a sighting alone does not establish that it is causing serious plant damage.

sources.label: Watson: Diaspididae of the World—Froggattiella penicillata
Kim et al. 2023: Newly recorded armoured scale insects in Korea

scirtothrips-perseae.summary: Avocado thrips is a small, straw-yellow insect that feeds on tender avocado leaves and young fruit. Fine dark lines cross the adult's abdomen, and the young are pale yellow. Feeding may bronze the leaves and leave rough brown scars on fruit as it grows, reducing its market quality even when the flesh remains usable. In California the insect became a major orchard pest after discovery in 1996. It often builds up during cooler periods when suitable young growth is available.

sources.label: USDA ARS: Scirtothrips perseae, a new species

sagina-subulata.summary: Awl-leaf pearlwort, often sold as Irish moss, is a low flowering perennial that forms dense green mats. Its slender stems root where they touch the ground, and pairs of fine leaves give it a mosslike appearance. Tiny white flowers rise just above the foliage in summer. It grows best in cool, moist conditions and is often planted between paving stones or in rock gardens. Despite the familiar nursery name, it is a flowering plant rather than a true moss.

axis-axis.summary: Axis deer is a spotted deer native to the Indian subcontinent, also known as chital. Adults retain white spots on a reddish-brown coat, and mature males usually carry three-pointed antlers. These social animals use woodland with grassy openings and access to water, feeding mainly on grasses but also browsing other vegetation. Introduced herds occur in places including Texas and Hawaii. In Texas, their ability to use limited forage can bring them into competition with native white-tailed deer.

stephanitis-pyrioides.summary: Azalea lace bug is a tiny insect with patterned, lace-like wings that feeds beneath azalea and rhododendron leaves. The upper surface develops pale speckles, while dark waste spots and shed skins collect underneath. Young bugs lack full wings and become dark and spiny as they grow. Eggs can remain in leaves through winter, allowing new generations to appear the next growing season. Heavy feeding can turn foliage almost white or brown, although visible damage does not always mean the shrub is dying.

sources.label: Oregon State: Azalea Lace Bug, EM9066

myosotis-azorica.summary: Myosotis azorica is a forget-me-not native to the Azores, where it is a conservation concern. This upright, branching herb has simple, fleshy leaves covered with hairs and clusters of small dark-blue to violet flowers at the ends of its stems. Each flower has five petals. It grows in moist places, including rough slopes near waterfalls. Grazing can threaten its remaining habitat. Its presence in this catalog should not be read as a reason to remove a rare native plant.

tagetes-erecta.summary: Aztec marigold is an upright annual from Mexico and Guatemala, widely grown for its large flower heads. Cultivated forms often have rounded clusters of yellow, orange or cream flowers above divided, aromatic leaves. Plant height varies greatly with the variety, from compact bedding plants to taller cut-flower types. It favors sunny, well-drained places and flowers through much of the warm season. The familiar names African marigold and American marigold refer to the same species and do not describe its native range.

nicotiana-rustica.summary: Aztec tobacco is an annual tobacco plant with broad, rounded leaves and relatively short, yellowish tubular flowers. Its foliage is noticeably wider than that of several other tobacco species. Native to Peru according to Kew's botanical account, it has been introduced across many regions, including parts of North America. It has a long history of ceremonial and medicinal use among some Indigenous peoples. Those cultural uses are part of its history, rather than advice to smoke, eat or prepare the plant.

gypsophila-paniculata.summary: Baby's breath is a branching perennial best known for the many tiny white flowers used in bouquets. Its open flower clusters rise above a leafy base and give the whole plant a rounded outline. Native across parts of Europe and temperate Asia, it favors sunny, well-drained sites and occurs along roadsides, fields and sandy ground. Garden escapes have become troublesome in some North American regions, including Great Lakes landscapes. The large, fleshy root helps established plants persist from year to year.

renibacterium-salmoninarum.summary: Bacterial kidney disease is a slow-developing infection of salmon, trout and related fishes caused by Renibacterium salmoninarum. It can affect wild fish as well as those raised in hatcheries. Some infected fish show swollen organs, skin sores or bulging eyes, while others carry the bacterium without obvious illness. Infection can pass between fish and from parents through eggs. Because these signs resemble other diseases and healthy-looking carriers occur, laboratory testing is needed to identify the cause reliably.

sources.label: Delghandi et al.: Renibacterium salmoninarum review
USGS: Bacterial Diseases of Wild Fish

bagrada-hilaris.summary: Bagrada bug is a small shield-shaped insect, black with orange and white markings. Both adults and young feed by piercing plants, with cabbage, broccoli and other mustard-family crops especially vulnerable. Feeding on seedlings can leave pale patches, distort developing leaves or destroy the growing tip. The bugs also use wild plants around fields, moving into crops as conditions change. Originally from parts of Africa and Asia, this species has become an agricultural pest in California and other introduced regions.

paspalum-notatum-var-saurae.summary: Paspalum notatum var. saurae is a name used for a perennial South American pasture grass, including the familiar Pensacola bahiagrass. Pensacola has narrow leaves, produces seed readily and can persist under heavy grazing. These traits helped make it a useful pasture grass in Florida. The name needs care: some botanical sources treat this variety as the separate species Paspalum saurae. Descriptions of broad-leaved bahiagrass cultivars should not automatically be applied to this narrower-leaved form.

sources.label: Kew POWO: Paspalum notatum var. saurae
Flora Uruguaya: Paspalum notatum var. saurae
Pensacola bahiagrass population dynamics in an eight-year grazed sward

bromus-racemosus.summary: Bald brome is a short-lived grass that grows as a loose tuft or sometimes as a single upright stem. Its leaves and lower sheaths are hairy, while the flower clusters carry several pale-green, many-flowered spikelets with slender bristles. It is native across a broad temperate range from the Azores and Europe into Asia, and has been introduced elsewhere. Although its common name suggests a hairless plant, the floral details, rather than the absence of leaf hairs, are important for identification.

sources.label: Flora of New Zealand: Bromus racemosus

impatiens-balfourii.summary: Balfour's touch-me-not is an annual with upright, branching stems and two-toned pink and white flowers. Each flower has a narrow spur extending behind it, and the pointed leaves have regularly toothed edges. Native to the western Himalayas, it has been grown as a garden ornamental and sometimes escapes into disturbed ground. In Victoria, Australia, botanical accounts describe localized dense stands near old gardens. Its smooth stems and modest flower size help separate it from some larger, more familiar balsams.

sources.label: Vienna Natural History Museum: Impatiens balfourii

neslia-paniculata.summary: Ballmustard is an annual mustard-family plant of fields, meadows and disturbed ground. Small yellow flowers are followed by rounded fruits, giving the seed-bearing stems their distinctive beadlike appearance. Native to Eurasia, it has spread into parts of northern North America, including New England. The seeds can be difficult to separate from harvested canola or mustard because they are similar in size. That makes it relevant as an agricultural weed even where it is less conspicuous than larger flowering plants.

cardiospermum-halicacabum.summary: Balloon vine is a tendril-climbing plant named for its inflated, papery fruit capsules. The green capsules become brown as they mature, enclosing black seeds with a pale heart-shaped mark. Divided leaves and small white flowers grow along branching stems that scramble over nearby plants. It occurs across tropical and subtropical regions in thickets, river margins and disturbed ground. In parts of the southeastern United States, introduced growth can cover surrounding vegetation, but its native and introduced status varies around the world.

platycodon-grandiflorus.summary: Balloon-flower is a perennial grown for buds that swell like small balloons before opening into broad, five-pointed bells. The flowers face outward or upward above leafy stems, appearing in late spring and summer. Native to eastern Asia, the plant returns from a fleshy root system that can be easily damaged by disturbance. It is commonly grown in sunny or partly shaded borders with well-drained soil. Its unusual unopened buds are usually the easiest feature to recognize.

adelges-piceae.summary: Balsam woolly adelgid is a tiny sap-feeding insect hidden beneath white, woolly wax on true fir trees. Colonies settle on bark and branches, where their feeding can cause swollen twigs, distorted growth and declining crowns. Susceptibility varies among fir species: Fraser fir in the southern Appalachians and subalpine fir in the western United States can suffer severe damage. Introduced from Europe, the insect reproduces without mating in North America. Its small size means an infestation may go unnoticed until tree symptoms develop.

momordica-charantia.summary: Balsampear, also called bitter melon, is a fast-growing annual vine with curling tendrils and deeply lobed leaves. Yellow flowers develop into bumpy or ridged fruits that change from green to orange when ripe. The mature fruit splits open, exposing seeds wrapped in bright red flesh. Cultivated varieties are familiar vegetables in many warm regions, while smaller-fruited forms may grow outside gardens. The plant thrives in heat and humidity and can climb supports or spread across the ground.

phyllostachys-reticulata.summary: This bamboo, also known as timber bamboo or Phyllostachys bambusoides, is a tall woody grass native to central and southern China. Its green canes carry long branches and pointed leaves that are bright green above and blue-green beneath. Young cane sheaths can be pinkish with purple mottling, a useful seasonal detail. It has a long history in cultivation, and its eventual size varies greatly with climate and growing conditions. The scientific name is more informative than the catalog's general label Bamboo.

sources.label: Trees and Shrubs Online: Phyllostachys reticulata

poliaspoides-formosana.summary: Bamboo armored scale is a small scale insect that can remain well hidden on its host. Recorded colonies occupy the tight space between a bamboo leaf stalk and the stem, so an ordinary glance at the leaves may miss them. The species was originally described from Asian bamboo and has since been reported in other regions, including Saint Lucia. Closely related scales require microscopic comparison, making the host and concealed feeding site useful search clues rather than a complete identification.

sources.label: Malumphy 2014: Scale insects of Saint Lucia

bambusaspis-bambusae.summary: Bamboo pit scale is a tiny sap-feeding insect found on bamboo leaves and stems. Females are elongated and yellowish, sheltered beneath a translucent cover that can blend into the plant. A fringe of pale wax may help reveal a colony. Observers in the Canary Islands found it on both leaf surfaces and stems, sometimes in large groups. It was considered a minor pest in that setting, so the number of scales alone should not be treated as proof of serious damage.

sources.label: Soria, Del Estal and Viñuela 1998: Asterolecaniidae in Spain

dinoderus-minutus.summary: Bamboo powderpost beetle develops inside cut bamboo, where both adults and larvae make feeding tunnels. The insects can attack culms during processing, storage or use, turning internal tissue into fine powder and reducing the material's strength. Eggs are laid inside the bamboo, and the young remain concealed as they grow. Fresh powder and small exit holes may reveal an infestation before the beetles themselves are noticed. Research in Japan documents it as an important pest of dried bamboo products.

sources.label: Watanabe et al. 2020: Bamboo beetle oviposition study
Garcia and Morrell 2009: Development at constant temperatures

stigmaeopsis-celarius.summary: Stigmaeopsis celarius is a tiny bamboo-feeding spider mite that lives beneath silk shelters on leaves. The dense, oval roofs cover small colonies and help protect them from predators. Behavioral experiments found that adults defend these nests and that larger groups provide stronger protection. Several related bamboo mites look similar and older reports used this name more broadly. Webbing beneath a bamboo leaf is therefore a useful place to look, but microscopic examination is needed to identify the species reliably.

sources.label: Saito and colleagues 2004: Reinstatement of Stigmaeopsis
Mori and Saito: Cooperative defense in a social spider mite
Zhang, Zhang and Lin (2000): Mites of Schizotetranychus from moso bamboo in Fujian, China

pentalonia-nigronervosa.summary: Banana aphid is a small, shiny brown to nearly black insect that feeds on banana sap. Colonies produce sticky honeydew, which can attract ants and support black sooty mold. Its greatest importance is as a carrier of banana bunchy top virus, rather than the feeding injury alone. Winged forms can disperse to other plants. Older accounts assigned aphids from ginger and several other hosts to this species, but modern research separates many of those populations as Pentalonia caladii.

sources.label: Foottit et al. 2010: Identity of Pentalonia species

opogona-sacchari.summary: Banana bud moth is a small brown moth whose caterpillars tunnel inside stems and other plant tissues. Despite its name, it attacks many plants, including palms, dracaenas, bananas and other tropical ornamentals. The pale caterpillars have a brown head and produce piles of fine plant waste held together with silk. Infested stems may weaken or collapse, and empty pupal cases can project from the tunnels. Damaged or stressed plants are especially attractive places for the nocturnal adults to lay eggs.

sources.label: University of Hawaii: Banana Moth BMP

pestalotiopsis-disseminata.summary: Pestalotiopsis disseminata is a fungus reported from many kinds of plants, sometimes causing blight, cankers or fruit decay and sometimes living within apparently healthy tissue. Symptoms depend on the host and growing conditions, so a spotted leaf alone does not identify it. A banana disease reference lists this species with fruit rot, while other Pestalotiopsis species are associated with banana leaf spots. Modern diagnosis combines microscopic characters with genetic evidence because older identifications based only on appearance can be unreliable.

sources.label: EFSA 2023: Pest categorisation of Pestalotiopsis disseminata
Keith et al. 2006: Identification and characterization of Pestalotiopsis species causing scab disease of guava

passiflora-tarminiana.summary: Banana passionflower is a climbing vine with three-lobed leaves, hanging pink flowers and elongated fruits that ripen yellow. Often called banana poka in Hawaii, it can climb high into forest vegetation and spread across tree crowns. Birds and pigs disperse its seeds there. The vine is native to the Andes and was long confused with another banana passionfruit, Passiflora mollissima. Its vigorous growth is a serious problem in some Hawaiian forests, where it can smother the plants supporting it.

heros-severus.summary: Banded cichlid is a deep-bodied South American fish from the upper Orinoco and upper Negro river regions. Dark vertical markings cross the body, but the pattern must be interpreted carefully because several related fishes are sold as severums. In the modern identification of Heros severus, one middle body bar is shortened rather than extending fully between the upper and lower fins. Older aquarium and biological accounts can mix it with other Heros species, making confirmed identity especially important.

scolytus-schevyrewi.summary: The banded elm bark beetle is a small Asian beetle that now occurs in North America. Adults are reddish brown with a darker band across the wing covers. Its pale, legless larvae tunnel beneath the bark of stressed elms, interrupting the tissues that move food through the tree. The beetle can also carry the fungus responsible for Dutch elm disease. Tree condition matters: in Utah, attacks on the common Siberian elm often cause little damage when disease is absent.

sources.label: Lee et al. 2011: Biology in the western United States

aloe-vera.summary: Barbados aloe is an evergreen succulent with a rosette of thick, pointed leaves edged with small pale teeth. The leaves store water and contain the clear gel familiar from cosmetic products. Mature plants can send up tall stalks bearing tubular yellow to orange flowers, while young offsets form beside the parent plant. It is widely grown in pots and warm-climate gardens, where freely draining soil is important. The yellow latex near the leaf surface differs from the inner gel and should not be casually consumed.

pereskia-aculeata.summary: Barbados gooseberry is a climbing cactus with ordinary-looking, slightly fleshy leaves. Paired hooked spines help its branches catch surrounding plants, while older stems carry clusters of longer spines. Fragrant white or pale-yellow flowers are followed by round yellow to orange fruits. Native to tropical America, it has escaped from gardens in places such as eastern Australia, where heavy, tangled growth can smother other vegetation. Broken stems and even leaves can regrow, making dumped garden material a source of new plants.

jatropha-curcas.summary: Barbados nut is a spreading shrub or small tree native to tropical America. Its broad leaves have three or five pointed lobes, and small yellow-green flowers develop into rounded capsules that split as they mature. The dark seeds contain oil used in industrial products and investigated as a fuel source. The plant tolerates drought and relatively poor soil, which has encouraged cultivation far beyond its native range. Despite the common name, its seeds are not edible nuts and can cause poisoning.

opuntia-ficus-indica.summary: Barbary fig is a large, branching cactus grown for its fleshy fruit. Its flattened, oval pads are stems, often forming a small tree with a distinct trunk. Many cultivated plants lack long spines, but small irritating bristles can still be present. Yellow flowers develop into rounded fruits that change color as they ripen. The species comes from Mexico and has been carried widely in cultivation. In New South Wales it sometimes escapes into surrounding vegetation, spreading through seeds and fallen stem pieces.

aegilops-triuncialis.summary: Barbed goatgrass is a winter annual grass closely related to wheat. Its stiff, narrow leaves and short seed heads become especially noticeable when the very long bristles spread from the developing seeds. Native from the Mediterranean region into central Asia, it grows in California grasslands, rangelands and oak woodlands, including some dry, shallow soils. The bristles catch on clothing and animal fur, helping seeds travel. They can also lodge around livestock mouths or eyes, reducing the usefulness of affected pasture.

gerbera-jamesonii.summary: Barberton daisy is a perennial from southern Africa with bold daisy-like flower heads held above a low rosette of leaves. The leaves are elongated and often deeply lobed, while the flowers usually have red outer rays surrounding a darker center. This species helped give rise to the many hybrid gerberas sold as bedding plants and cut flowers. It favors bright conditions and moist but well-drained soil; saturated soil can damage its roots. In colder climates it is commonly grown seasonally or protected from frost.

cryptocarenus-heveae.summary: Cryptocarenus heveae is a very small, dark-brown bark beetle recorded in South America. At roughly two millimeters long, it is difficult to recognize without a microscope. A specialist key uses details of the forehead, including a shallow depression and small central bump, to separate it from similar beetles. Researchers have caught it in ethanol-baited traps in a mixed Brazil-nut and rubber plantation in the southern Amazon. That finding documents its presence there, but does not by itself show which trees it was using.

sources.label: Revista Mexicana de Biodiversidad: Illustrated scolytine keys
Monteiro, Garlet and Carvalho 2019: Plantation beetle survey

xylosandrus-germanus.summary: The black stem borer is a tiny ambrosia beetle from eastern Asia that has become a pest of orchard and nursery trees in North America. Females are shiny black and about two millimeters long. They bore into trunks or branches and grow a fungus inside their tunnels as food for themselves and their young. Stressed trees are especially attractive. Small entry holes, sometimes with thin toothpick-like strands of sawdust, may be easier to notice than the beetles themselves. Heavy attacks can accompany wilting and decline.

sources.label: Halliday et al.: Field Guide to Ambrosia Beetles

echinochloa-crus-galli.summary: Barnyardgrass is a variable annual grass common in damp, disturbed ground and cultivated fields. Its flattened stems may spread near the ground before turning upward, carrying broad, flat blades. The branched seed head is crowded with small spikelets and may have a purplish cast. One useful clue is the absence of a small membrane or fringe where the leaf blade meets its sheath. Introduced from Eurasia into North America, it is a familiar agricultural weed of irrigated fields, ditches and rice-growing areas.

peronospora-belbahrii.summary: Basil downy mildew is caused by Peronospora belbahrii, a microscopic water mold that infects basil. Leaves often turn yellow between the main veins, while gray to purple downy growth develops underneath. Symptoms may begin low on the plant and spread upward, making a healthy-looking crop decline quickly in humid conditions. The pathogen can arrive on seed or infected plants, and its spores travel through the air. Yellowing alone can resemble a nutrient problem, so the leaf underside provides an important clue.

sources.label: University of Minnesota: Basil downy mildew
Gevens: Wisconsin Vegetable Crop Update, July 27 2025

callisia-fragrans.summary: Basket plant is a fleshy perennial from Mexico that forms clusters of broad, glossy leaves. Long flowering stalks rise from the upper leaf bases and carry small, fragrant white flowers. Some cultivated forms have pale or purple markings, so leaf color alone is unreliable. Grown as an ornamental groundcover, it has escaped into hammocks and disturbed places in central and southern Florida, where it can displace existing vegetation. A plant growing outside cultivation should be assessed in its local setting before removal is planned.

thrips-calcaratus.summary: Basswood thrips is a small, brown insect associated mainly with lindens and basswoods. Adults have narrow wings, and identifying them precisely requires microscopic details such as a tiny curved claw on the front foot. The insect feeds on young developing buds and leaves. Native to Europe, it has become a forest pest in the upper Midwest, where outbreaks can cause extensive loss of basswood foliage. Its early-season feeding can leave damage that is mistaken for frost injury rather than insect activity.

sources.label: Rieske and Raffa 1996: Bionomics and host range
Raffa 1991: Biology and impact in Great Lakes region

sphagneticola-trilobata.summary: Bay Biscayne creeping oxeye, also called wedelia, is a fast-spreading groundcover with fleshy leaves and bright yellow daisy-like flowers. Its rounded stems creep along the ground and can form dense mats. Native to tropical America, it was planted widely for its flowers and rapid cover. In Florida, garden escapes now occur beside streams, roads and other disturbed places, where thick growth crowds neighboring plants. Runners and broken pieces are particularly important in its spread, so cutting a patch can scatter material capable of growing again.

sources.label: UF/IFAS Center for Aquatic and Invasive Plants: Sphagneticola trilobata

bean-common-mosaic-necrosis-virus.summary: Bean common mosaic necrosis virus is a plant virus that affects beans and related legumes. It can produce mottled, distorted leaves, but the result depends strongly on the bean variety. In some varieties, infection triggers darkening veins, wilt and widespread tissue death; in others it resembles ordinary bean common mosaic. Infected seed can introduce the virus, and aphids spread it between plants during brief feeding visits. Because related viruses can cause similar symptoms, laboratory testing is needed to distinguish them reliably.

sources.label: Jordan and Hammond 2020: BCMV and BCMNV
